summary.text: Leela Gray is the Democratic nominee in Florida's 13th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army Brigadier General with 30 years of service, she is also a lawyer; she won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 65.1% of the vote. She is running on affordability, government ethics, and support for veterans and seniors.

paragraphs.text: Gray says her family relied on food stamps while she was growing up and that she worked two jobs to pay for college.
She earned a bachelor's degree from Elon University, a graduate degree from the U.S. Army War College, and a law degree from the Stetson University College of Law.
She served in the U.S. Army from 1988 to 2018, rising to the rank of Brigadier General.

According to an EMILYs List endorsement release, Gray's Army career included commanding troops, a peacekeeping mission, and two combat deployments. After active duty she worked at the State Department as a strategic advisor to U.S. Army Cyber Command.
The same release describes her as a longtime Tampa Bay resident who has mentored entrepreneurs and advocated for veterans.
Gray defeated Brandt Robinson and John Liccione in the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 13th District.

sources.title: EMILYs List Endorses Retired Brigadier General Leela Gray for Florida's 13th Congressional District
